title: Shamonda virus in human - France

signal.disease: Shamonda virus disease (human infection)
signal.pathogen: Shamonda virus (SHAV), genus Orthobunyavirus, Simbu serogroup; genotype SHAV-EU1
signal.headline: France reports the world's first confirmed human Shamonda virus infection, a fatal encephalitis in an immunocompromised man. Source and route are unknown, and WHO cannot yet assess the risk.

signal.summary: On 20 October 2026, France notified WHO of the first laboratory-confirmed human Shamonda virus infection reported globally. The patient was an immunocompromised older man from rural eastern France who had not travelled in the preceding year. He developed neurological signs on 23 September, was diagnosed with severe encephalitis on 25 September and died on 8 October. SHAV was confirmed by metagenomics and RT-PCR, with very high viral loads in post-mortem tissue, and other encephalitis causes were excluded. No source of exposure was identified, although mosquito exposure was reported. Testing of blood donors linked to his transfusions was negative, so transfusion-associated transmission is unlikely but not fully excluded. SHAV is widespread in animals in Europe, and WHO says the human risk cannot yet be reliably assessed or quantified. No additional human cases have been detected to date.
